# Evidence Summary: Biochar Amendment and Wheat Yield Under Drought Stress

## Claim
Biochar amendment increases wheat yield under drought stress.

## Evidence

Research demonstrates that biochar application enhances crop productivity through multiple mechanisms that are particularly beneficial under water-limited conditions. A comprehensive meta-analysis of biochar effects across diverse agricultural systems found significant positive effects on crop yield, with the greatest benefits observed in soils with low fertility and acidic pH conditions where water stress often co-occurs [@jeffery2011meta]. These yield improvements are attributed to enhanced soil physical and biological properties.

The mechanisms underlying biochar's beneficial effects on crop performance involve improvements to soil structure and water retention capacity. Biochar amendment enhances soil biological activity and microbial communities [@lehmann2011biochar], which play critical roles in nutrient cycling and plant stress resilience. Additionally, biochar application improves soil fertility by increasing pH, cation exchange capacity, and nutrient availability [@novak2009ph], creating more favorable growing conditions that buffer plants against environmental stresses including drought.

These soil improvements are particularly relevant for wheat production under water-limited conditions, where enhanced water retention and nutrient availability can mitigate drought impacts on yield. The combination of improved soil physical properties, enhanced biological activity, and increased nutrient availability provides a mechanistic basis for biochar's capacity to support crop productivity under stress conditions.

## References

Jeffery, S., Verheijen, F. G. A., & van der Velde, M. (2011). A quantitative review of the effects of biochar application to soils on crop productivity using meta-analysis. *Agriculture, Ecosystems and Environment*, 144, 175–187.

Lehmann, J., Rillig, M. C., & Thies, J. (2011). Biochar effects on soil biota – A review. *Soil Biology and Biochemistry*, 43, 1812–1836.

Novak, J. M., Busscher, W. J., & Laird, D. L. (2009). Impact of biochar amendment on fertility of a southeastern coastal plain soil. *Soil Science*, 174, 105–112.
